previous_english_corrections.old_headline: Simulated quantum reservoirs trace memory to Liouvillian modes, dissipation and feedback
previous_english_corrections.old_summary: Five theory/simulation preprints ask how relaxation, dissipation and delayed feedback generate memory and nonlinearity in quantum reservoirs; none report experiments.
previous_english_corrections.old_synthesis: All five preprints are theoretical or numerical studies asking which physical dynamics of open quantum reservoirs produce task-relevant memory and nonlinear processing, and they give different answers. In driven-dissipative Kerr reservoirs, arxiv:2609.20345 finds enhanced memory near both first-order and continuous dissipative transitions. Its exact post-training Liouvillian-mode decomposition attributes capacity mainly to finite-rate modes and their cross-terms, with weak contribution from the gap mode. arxiv:2609.23429 proposes a Volterra-weight factorization W^(q)=BH^(q) separating input-history pathways from readout visibility, and argues that weak measurement and delayed feedback can activate otherwise invisible covariance modes. arxiv:2609.27072 proposes coherent waveguide-QED feedback to a Kerr resonator. In NARMA-n tasks, the optimal delay approximately tracks the input-product lag. In neutral-atom simulations, arxiv:2609.28441 finds controlled dissipation necessary for the echo-state property and reports Mackey-Glass solutions with N=5 atoms. arxiv:2609.22791 models a Gaussian cavity-magnomechanical reservoir with strong memory, limited nonlinearity, and a measurement-budget-dependent optimal encoding.
previous_english_corrections.new_headline: Models trace quantum reservoir memory to Liouvillian modes, dissipation and feedback
previous_english_corrections.new_summary: Theory and simulation preprints tie reservoir memory to model-specific causes: Liouvillian modes, evolution time, dissipation, coherent delayed feedback.
previous_english_corrections.new_synthesis: These theoretical and numerical preprints ask which mechanisms and control parameters set memory and nonlinear processing in quantum reservoirs. None reports an experimental measurement, and the answers differ by model. For driven-dissipative Kerr reservoirs, arXiv:2609.20345 finds enhanced memory and nonlinear processing near both first-order and continuous dissipative transitions. Its Liouvillian-mode decomposition attributes the gain mainly to finite-rate modes rather than the gap mode. arXiv:2609.23429 develops a Volterra-weight framework, W^(q)=BH^(q), and argues that thermalization shifts the response toward the most recent input. In that framework, weak measurement and delayed feedback can activate or return information. In a proposed waveguide-QED reservoir with a Kerr resonator, arXiv:2609.27072 reports that the optimal feedback delay approximately tracks the NARMA-n input-product lag. In a Gaussian cavity magnomechanical proposal, arXiv:2609.22791 finds that evolution time controls the balance between memory and nonlinear processing. In simulated neutral-atom arrays, arXiv:2609.28441 reports that controlled dissipation is necessary for fading memory and that performance peaks at the edge of quantum chaos.

interpretation.newly_ranked: The three dark energy studies estimate constant or evolving equation-of-state parameters using two supernova analyses and gravitational lensing. The binary studies evaluate photometric, astrometric and spectroscopic companion detection. The English copy distinguishes simulated accuracy, recall and companions ruled out. The three denominators support no common efficiency estimate.
interpretation.still_missing: The review separated the stellar benchmark catalogue from two pipelines and separated one rotation-period catalogue from two cluster studies. It split direct detection on full KiDS images from two crop-based lens searches. None of the intended three-paper sets ranked.
interpretation.retained_or_changed: Thirteen of twenty coherent September groups kept their exact membership. Four others gained a study, including one CMS tracking group and three groups interpreting the LZ recoil. The coupling and recoil-suppression groups lost one or more members. No paper from the former diffusion group ranked. The intact October false merge combines optical delay, broadband-phase and quantum Fisher information studies. No member of the fifteen previously justified exclusions appeared in a new rank.

synthesis.membership: Five original papers plus one study of self-interacting dark matter.
synthesis.assessment: The new text distinguishes which theoretical interpretations check relic abundance, solar capture and elastic scattering. The old universal constraint claim is absent.

synthesis.membership: Three of the four original papers.
synthesis.assessment: The shorter group no longer includes the conformally coupled study that reported a lower minimum chi-squared. The text gives the reported model comparison for each remaining study. Removing the fourth paper makes this a different comparison.

The synthesis softened the original claim to “activate or return information” but still left the intervention-to-outcome mapping ambiguous. Weak measurement exposes covariance modes. Delayed feedback creates return pathways for earlier inputs.

interpretation.decision: The prespecified requirement for an independent test passed. Two of five omissions ranked, and intact mixed controls fell from two to one. This authorized the August trials only.
